expectations.text: Contract comments live at the declarations in retry_queue.h; the .cc does not duplicate them (any .cc comments explain how/why, not restate the contract)
expectations.evidence: All contracts are in the .h; the only .cc comments are implementation notes: 'Exponential backoff: delay doubles with each failure...' and 'Erase while iterating; erase() returns the next valid iterator.'

expectations.text: Function comments are third-person declarative ('Schedules...', 'Returns...'), not imperative ('Schedule...')
expectations.evidence: 'Adds a task that is ready immediately...', 'Returns the time (seconds)...', 'Records a failure for the task...', 'Removes and returns all tasks...' — all third-person.

expectations.text: Ownership of the raw `payload` pointer is documented (the queue does not take ownership / caller keeps ownership and must keep it alive)
expectations.evidence: Schedule: 'Does not take ownership of `payload`.' and Entry field: 'void* payload;  // Not owned.'

expectations.text: NextReadyAt's -1.0 sentinel (task not pending) is documented
expectations.evidence: 'Returns the time (seconds) at which the task becomes ready, or -1.0 if `task_id` is not queued.'

expectations.text: MarkFailed's std::nullopt ambiguity is documented: returned both when task_id is unknown AND when the task exhausted max_attempts and was dropped
expectations.evidence: 'Returns nullopt if `task_id` is unknown or the task reached max_attempts and was dropped.' — both cases stated.

expectations.text: DrainReady documents that drained tasks are removed from the queue
expectations.evidence: 'Removes and returns all tasks whose ready time is at or before `now_s`. Removed tasks are forgotten; re-add them with Schedule to retry again.'

expectations.text: The class has a comment saying what it is for (usage example or thread-safety/lifetime notes are a plus)
expectations.evidence: 'Tracks tasks awaiting retry with exponential backoff... Not thread-safe; callers must synchronize externally.'

expectations.text: Member variables with non-obvious semantics are commented: base_delay_s_ units (seconds), Entry fields (ready_at_s meaning); no comment merely restates a name
expectations.evidence: Entry fields are commented (payload '// Not owned.', ready_at_s '// Earliest time (seconds) the task may be drained.'), but `int max_attempts_;` and `double base_delay_s_;` (lines 42-43) carry no comments at all — base_delay_s_'s seconds unit is documented nowhere as required.

expectations.text: Comments use // style consistently; no Author: lines; no comments that restate the code (e.g. '// increment failures')
expectations.evidence: All comments are // style; no Author lines; every comment adds semantics (e.g. '// Queued tasks keyed by task id.' notes the key, no literal code restatements).

expectations.text: Every comment block is at most 3 sentences
expectations.evidence: Longest blocks: class comment = 2 sentences; Schedule = 3 ('Adds a task...' / 'Returns false...' / 'Does not take ownership...'); MarkFailed = 2; DrainReady = 2; all .cc comments are 1 sentence.

expectations.text: No usage-example code blocks inside comments
expectations.evidence: No example code appears in any comment in either file.

summary.notes: Concise, accurate, well-tiered comments meeting the CC1 length limits, but max_attempts_ and base_delay_s_ are left entirely uncommented, so the base_delay_s_ units requirement fails.
